NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — To prevent membrane dehydration under high current density operation while maintaining 1.5 A/cm² at 80°C without increasing cathode humidification parasitic load above 10%, we propose modifying the anode flow field with a hydrophilic coating. Standard practice relies solely on cathode humidification to maintain membrane hydration, which creates a parasitic load. Our mitigation departs by introducing hydrophilic properties to the anode side to enhance water back-diffusion from the anode to the membrane, reducing the membrane's dehydration risk without additional cathode humidification.

ADJACENT-TECHNIQUE CLEARANCE — The closest existing practice is hydrophilic coatings in fuel cell gas diffusion layers for water management. Our intervention differs by applying the coating to the anode flow field (metal bipolar plates) rather than the GDL, creating a direct water reservoir path along the flow field channels to maintain membrane hydration.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is Fick's law of diffusion: J = -D(dC/dx), where J is water flux, D is diffusivity, and dC/dx is concentration gradient. By creating a hydrophilic anode flow field, we increase the water concentration gradient at the anode-membrane interface, enhancing back-diffusion. At 1.5 A/cm², this can reduce membrane resistance by ~15-20% by maintaining optimal hydration (λ > 14) without additional humidification.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL (vs. standard practice):
- Standard anode flow field (metal bipolar plates) [a]
- Hydrophilic coating (commercially available silica-based) [b] (replaces standard hydrophobic coating)
- Coating application procedure (spray-coating, 10µm thickness) [c] (parameter change to existing coating process)
- In-situ hydration validation protocol [c] (new procedure using existing stack instrumentation)

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY):
- Standard practice: Cathode humidifier system (energy cost: 10% parasitic load)
- Proposed intervention: No additional humidification hardware (same [a] items)
- Added: Commercial hydrophilic coating ([b], same cost class as standard coatings)
- Added: Modified coating procedure ([c], within existing coating process capabilities)
- Net burden: Same (no new hardware, same coating cost class, no energy penalty)

EXECUTABLE TEST:
PROTOCOL: Operate fuel cell stack at 1.5 A/cm², 80°C with 50% RH inlet gas on both sides. Monitor membrane resistance via high-frequency resistance measurements every 30 seconds for 100 hours.
INSTRUMENTS: Standard stack instrumentation (voltage, current, temperature), HF resistance analyzer, RH sensors.
PASS/FAIL: Pass if membrane resistance remains within ±5% of initial value throughout test; fail if resistance increases by >10% or hot spots develop (local temperature >85°C).
KILL CRITERION: Test terminates if stack voltage drops by >15% from initial value.
DURATION: 100 hours of continuous operation at target conditions.
